alignments.note: לָכֵן fused into the single English word 'Wherefore' (rule 30), headed on כֵּן as the lexeme-bearing morpheme.

Predicate adjective of the oath clause חַי־אָנִי. The ASV's fixed rendering of that formula is 'As ... live', and the supplied 'As' is what English spends on the adverbial force of this predicate rather than a conjunction supplied for a clause that lacks one (rule 20); the unit is discontinuous around the pronoun's own word (rule 25) and heads on 'live'. The corpus aligns חַי before a 1cs pronoun to 'as live' in six chapters, including EZK.16.48, EZK.20.3 and EZK.20.31. Marking the 'As' 'added' as a supplied subordinator under rule 55 is the competing reading; it was taken earlier in this chapter and is reversed here.
Explicit subject pronoun of the verbless oath clause takes only its own English word (rule 20); the corpus gives this pronoun 'I' alone in all eighteen units following the oath adjective.
Supplied 'the' belongs to the nominal expression it determines (rule 15).
The suffix of אֲדֹנָי is not separately rendered (rules 18, 22).

The oath formula אִם־לֹא is rendered by the single word 'surely'. The polarity reversal leaves neither morpheme's own sense in the English, so the phrase is genuinely indivisible (rule 6) rather than a compositional rule 30 fusion like this chapter's לָכֵן, מִשָּׁם and מִמֶּנּוּ; the corpus reads אִם־לֹא → 'surely' as noncompositional in six of seven two-token occurrences, the seventh (1KI.20.25) conceding the analysis in its own note. Source head is the first token as the deterministic display anchor (rule 6); heading on the negative, and keeping the unit 'aligned', are the competing readings.
Object marker with the object written bare (rule 16).
Finite verb with subject pronoun and auxiliary, headed on the lexical verb (rules 17, 24).
One substantive rendered by a multi-word English phrase; head on the lexeme-bearing word, 'things' being the supplied generic noun (rule 31).
Apodosis waw rendered by the connective 'therefore' (rule 14).
גַּם → also, standing postpositively; distance is not evidence against it (rules 51, 25).
Finite verb with its auxiliary, discontinuous around the pronoun and 'also' (rules 17, 25).
Italic supplied object; אֶגְרַע carries no object suffix, so the pronoun answers to no morpheme (rules 7, 44, 30).
Waw plus negative fused into 'neither' (rule 35), headed on the negative.
Finite verb with auxiliary, discontinuous around the subject noun phrase (rules 17, 25).
Verb rendered as a light verb plus complement, 'will have ... pity'; head on the complement (rule 44), the unit discontinuous around the negative (rule 25).

review_notes: Corrected at reconciliation: the 'as' of 'As I live' now belongs to חַי, whose unit is the discontinuous 'as ... live' headed on 'live'. The corpus aligns חַי before a 1cs pronoun to 'as live' in six chapters, three of them Ezekiel chapters using this same formula, and the pronoun keeps only its 'I'. The earlier reading, which made the word an added supplied subordinator under rule 55, is named in that unit's note and is closed by this chapter's amendment to rule 55.

Corrected at reconciliation: אִם־לֹא → 'surely' is restated noncompositional, with the same arrays and the same two heads. The polarity reversal makes the phrase indivisible under rule 6, and the corpus reads it that way in six of seven two-token occurrences, EZK.20.33 among them. The chapter's compositional fusions (לָכֵן, מִשָּׁם, מִמֶּנּוּ) are untouched and remain aligned.
Unchanged: the italic 'thee' after 'diminish' stays added, אֶגְרַע carrying no object suffix; and the two גַּם keep the 'also' the ASV writes for each.
